texts.preamble: Pawan Kumar Surana & Ors vs Bishnu Prasad Samanta on 12 January, 2017
texts.arguments: It is submitted by Mr. Roy, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners that the present accused persons, namely, Pawan Kumar Surana, Shanti Kumar Surana and Vijay Dwivedi ought not to have been implicated in Complaint Case No.6D of 2010, now pending before the learned Municipal Magistrate and Metropolitan Magistrate, 3rd Court, Calcutta under Section 16(1)a (i) and under Section 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. He took me to running page no. 20 to show that one Joydeep Nath (accused no. 1), Operation Head of M/s. Middleton Hotels Pvt. Ltd. was nominated by the company by a Resolution passed at their meeting held on 22/12/2008 at Kolkata to be a person in charge and responsible to the said company for the conduct of the business of the said company or establishment. He further submitted that the said application was received by the Chief Municipal Health Officer, Kolkata on 02/01/2009 and in view of Sections 17(2) and Rule 12(b) of the said Act, no prosecution can be maintainable as against these petitioners who are admittedly the directors of the said Private Limited Company. Mr. Roy has also relied up the decisions of the Apex Court as reported in 1983 SCC (Cri) 115 (Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs. Ram Kishan Rohtagi And Others), (2011) 1 SCC (Cri) 8 (Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited Vs. Food Inspector And Another) and 1992 SCC (Cri) 412 (R. Banerjee And Others Vs. H. D. Dubey And Others) in support of his claim that if the company nominates any person under Rule 12(b) of the said Act, then only the said person will be responsible for the conduct of the business of the said company and the directors cannot be arraigned for any Pawan Kumar Surana & Ors vs Bishnu Prasad Samanta on 12 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15810846/ 1 offence committed under the said Act. It is submitted by Mr. Das, learned Advocate, representing the Kolkata Municipal Corporation by taking me to paragraph 16 of the application to convince this court that one petition was filed before the learned trial court by the petitioner no. 3 that some goods were purchased by that hotel from Anand Trading Company. He submitted that under Section 14A of the said Act, this petitioner no. 3 tried to escape the legal liability. Mr. Das contended that the said petition has not been annexed and that was necessary for appreciation of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further contended that no copy of the resolution of the meeting of the company held on 22/12/2008 was produced before the learned trial court or the said resolution was not annexed with the Form No. VIII (Annexure-P-4). He further submitted that there is no address of the said Joydeep Nath appearing in that Form No. VIII. In reply, it is submitted by Mr. Roy that the name of Joydeep Nath is very much there in the said Form as Operation Head of M/s. Middleton Hotels Pvt. Ltd. and that is enough address to track a person. The decision of Kerala High Court as reported in 2010 Cr.L.J. (NOC) 496 Kerala is not enough to give a go-bye to the three decisions of the Apex Court as referred to above which are squarely on the point as involved in this case.
